scope: Local VRMA orders only; estimate remains maximum. Finalize when Operator confirms outbound load, not on packing.
specApproval: not obtained (autonomous run); user explicitly confirmed local-only scope and upper bound

setup.testEnvironment: isolated standard Compose, mbbs-tests.slice, bounded resources, teardown trap before launch
setup.production: User requested old short-loaded local VRMA balances disappear. Stage and test scoped live-source release; audit and repair eligible historical orders after deployment.

scenarios: Estimate 100, packed 80: final quantity and loaded quantity 80; abandon 20; Loaded status, no remainder.
Untouched line estimate 40 becomes zero with abandoned 40, retained in history.
Original estimate and abandoned amount survive in load proof and audit.
Confirming or editing packing alone preserves estimate and open balance.
Estimate is maximum; sales-only and converted packaging remain capped.
Converted rounding shortage is actual loaded quantity, never rounded up to the estimate.
Prior partial load plus new load becomes cumulative final quantity.
Empty load rejects; duplicate/concurrent load produces one durable record.
Storage failure rolls back quantities, status, history and audit together.
Sales and transfer partial loading still retain their balances; no inventory or NetSuite writes.
SCM can complete finalized VRMA without forced quantity override.
Operator confirmation explains abandonment for local VRMA and retains existing wording for other orders.
Converted local VRMA overages smaller than normal rounding tolerance are rejected.
SCM schedule displays actual finalized quantity and weight.

Historical short-loaded local VRMA with proof, no active packing and no consolidation claim is finalized to already-loaded quantity; audit retains all prior lines; dry-run does not mutate; rerun does nothing.
Historical orders with active packing or no proof, and other order types, are excluded from cleanup.
Sales-only PLT estimate 100 and load 80 preserves final quantity 80 and Dispatch pallet count 80.
Historical maintenance rejects omitted, empty, or greater-than-500 reference lists.
